claim: R4-13 made the disaster's unit count two-stage. §10.2 (c) (l. 15631–15635) keeps round(s × n) clamped to [1, n] as every place's count, and then "the `neighbourhoods` place … draws at least every matched target (max(k, |`matched`|)) and, by fire, stops where its order ends, the shortfall reported (V01 §3.16 (5))". V01 §3.16 (5) (l. 2361–2366), the home, takes "the first max(k, |`matched`|) units of the order — all of a shorter fire order". V12 l. 2709 agrees. V07 §5.6 (1) (l. 3411–3415) still equates the look's units with the first stage: "A look scaled as a share of its place's units (§10.2 (c)) takes … round(s × n) clamped to [1, n] where s is above 0 and none where it is not — V01 §3.16 (5)'s count of the disaster's units, read for every share at the village rungs". T-V7-69 (c) bars the same ("a look scaled as a share of its place's n units at share s takes round(s × n) clamped to [1, n] where s is above 0"). Take a VILLAGE of four ends and a calamity naming two of them at severity 0: s = 0.05, so k = round(0.2) clamped to 1. V07 strikes one end, V01 strikes both, and a correct build fails T-V7-69 (c). A fire whose order ends before k gives a third outcome. R4-13's routing named only pipeline and V12. Two units, two outcomes for one case (R3-03 (b)).
required_change: V07 §5.6 (1): after "… round(s × n) clamped to [1, n] where s is above 0 and none where it is not" replace "— V01 §3.16 (5)'s count of the disaster's units, read for every share at the village rungs," with "— §10.2 (c)'s count k, read for every share at the village rungs," and, after "… never rounds to nothing", add: "; the disaster's `neighbourhoods` place then strikes at least every matched target — the first max(k, |`matched`|) units of its order — and, by fire, stops where its order ends, the shortfall reported (V01 §3.16 (5), the home)". T-V7-69 (c): after "… takes round(s × n) clamped to [1, n] where s is above 0" add "— a disaster's units the first max(k, |`matched`|) of its order, k that count, or all of a shorter fire order (V01 §3.16 (5)) — on a VILLAGE fixture whose calamity names more ends than k (every named end struck) and on a fire whose order ends before k (the shortfall reported)".

claim: R4-12: "Every Find reader at a drawn week reads that listing over the model the view draws". §11.2 *At a drawn week* (l. 16455–16463) makes the listing the frame's ("every row, count, match and gap unit") wherever that week's frame is not the head. V01 §5.4, the town's reading, now reads the frame (lead l. 3139–3142; (1) l. 3167–3171; (3) l. 3188–3191; (4) a change of the drawn week re-evaluates). V01 §5.4's lead hands the village rungs to V07 §5.5 ("Below TOWN the village's reading is V07 §5.5's"), and V09 §4.21.10 (3) and (10) read V07 §5.5 there. V07 §5.5 (1) (l. 3339) builds the list "by §11.2's gazetteer query over the committed records", and W83 (l. 291) says the same. (2)'s gap units are the ends with no date. (4) re-evaluates on "Every commit, regenerate, undo, village epoch and hand-off" but not on a change of the drawn week. T-V7-68 runs no scrubbed week. So at a scrubbed VILLAGE week whose frame is not the head, one builder lists, glows and gaps the head's ends and uses (V07), and another the frame's (§11.2, V01). Examples are a smithy an epoch opened after that week, or two ends merged since. This is the class R4-12 graded major (VRC3T-01, VV12-r3-03, VAL-R3-05); R4-12's sweep did not reach V07.
required_change: V07 §5.5 (1): "built by §11.2's gazetteer query over the committed records" → "built by §11.2's gazetteer query over the model the view draws — the committed head or, at a drawn week (§2.9's `week`) whose frame is not the head, V06 §3.15.2's frame (§11.2's *At a drawn week*) —"; its **areas** bullet adds "at such a week, the ends and field groups that frame holds". (2) adds: "At a drawn week whose frame is not the head, the units and their members are read over that frame (§11.2's *At a drawn week*; V01 §5.4 (3)): an end the frame lacks is no unit." (4): "Every commit, regenerate, undo, village epoch and hand-off re-evaluates the chips at once" → "Every commit, regenerate, undo, village epoch and hand-off, and every change of the view's drawn week (§2.9's `week`), re-evaluates the chips at once". W83's input cell "§11.2's gazetteer at the view's effective key over the committed records" → "§11.2's gazetteer at the view's effective key and drawn week (§11.2's *At a drawn week*; V06 §3.15.2's frame)". T-V7-68 adds: "at a scrubbed week whose frame is not the head, on a VILLAGE fixture whose later epoch opened a smithy, closed another's use and merged two ends, each chip's matches, the ends listed and Show gaps' units equal §11.2's listing at that week, and the head's are back at the head". Its timing cell adds "its scrubbed-week clause at the first exit after M6-E's history frames (V06 §8, E6)".

claim: Village tracks cross a raised way by a different rule from the base's. R4-09 made §4.3 *Lattice and costs* (l. 5623-5634) the one crossing rule for ground part 0. A standing raised way's support rings, ramps, stairs and feet, and the under-deck strips of its `vault` spans, are 'impassable to every route and growth proposal on ground part 0' after generation, and at generation where the raised way is held (a declared one is). Elsewhere its strip is crossed only under an `open` span whose clear width is at least the way's width + `clearWidthM` and whose soffit meets *The clearance*, within ± `squareDeg` of square, never along the strip. §4.3 calls this 'the one rule S5c's proposals (§4.4) and stage 2's ways (V01 §3.17.3 (3)) keep'. V07 §3.5a (3) gives VS4's trackers, which are growth proposals on ground part 0, a different rule. Only supports whose `state` is absent or `ruined` are obstacles, and 'A tracker passes beneath a span, standing, ruined or cleared, freely: no junction, no crossing record, no gate, no stop'. Nothing stops a tracker at a ramp or a stair. V07 (7) registers V04's arch-vault source at every village rung, and a `vault` span inside the perimeter holds an arch vault (`storage`). So on a village map with a declared or carried-down raised way, a VS4 track can run through an arch vault chamber, over a ramp, or at any angle under a span too low for it. The base forbids each of these, and V04's T-V4-62 bars an arch vault 'over a part-0 way' at every rung. Two outcomes for one case.
required_change: V07 §3.5a (3): *Supports are obstacles* reads 'A support whose `state` is absent or `ruined`, the raised way's ramps and stairs, and the under-deck strip of each `vault` span (impassable by §4.3 *Lattice and costs*), each grown by `raised.supportClearM` (1 m), is an obstacle …', the turn rule unchanged. *Under a span* reads 'A tracker crosses the under-deck strip only where §4.3 *Lattice and costs* admits a part-0 way — under an `open` span whose clear width is at least the way's width + `raisedWays.structure.clearWidthM` and whose soffit meets §2.7's *The clearance* for the way's class, within ± `raisedWays.structure.squareDeg` of square to the deck, never along the strip. A step that would enter the strip elsewhere turns by the rule above. Where it crosses there is no junction, no crossing record, no gate and no stop; a `cleared` span's ground is free ((2)).' T-V7-48 adds '0 VS4 ways on a ramp, a stair or a `vault` span's under-deck strip or along the strip, each VS4 way crossing a span under an `open` span within §4.3's clear width, clearance and `squareDeg`'. Pipeline's END: §4.3's '— the one rule S5c's proposals (§4.4) and stage 2's ways (V01 §3.17.3 (3)) keep' adds 'and V07 §3.5a (3)'s village trackers'.

claim: A crossing station carried down onto the village palisade gets two outcomes. At the hand-off down 'the standing fabric survives unchanged' and the palisade is 'the innermost standing enceinte' (V07 §3.12). A CITY's raised way stays through the fall (V07 §3.5a's lead; V06 §3.19). Where a viaduct or elevated road crossed that ring, §2.7's support step (3) gave it a crossing station: a raised gate 'whose tower carries the deck', and a station whose support is the band's stretch under the deck, held while the deck stands (§4.8 *Gates*). V07 rules the opposite for every raised way over the palisade, declared or carried down. §3.5a (4) says the support is 'never a gate … a raised way crossing the circuit makes no gate'. §3.17's row 'a raised way over the palisade' says 'no gate under the deck'. T-V7-48, on a fixture 'carried down from a CITY', bars that the palisade 'has 0 gates at supports'. §2.7 (6) (b) (iv), new this round, says the same of a palisade laid later. Nothing states what happens to the standing raised gate and its station. One builder keeps them (base (3); standing fabric). Another removes the gate, which leaves the deck on no support, or fails T-V7-48 on a correct build. §3.17's row also cites T-V7-52, the no-op pins, for this case.
required_change: V07 §3.5a (4) adds: 'A raised way carried down (V07 §3.12) whose crossing station stands on the enceinte that becomes the palisade keeps that station as standing fabric — its support the band's stretch under the deck, held while the deck stands, with its raised gate whose tower carries the deck, or the aqueduct's arch (§2.7's support step (3)) — the one gate at a support the palisade carries; the abutting and no-gate rule above reads every other support in its band.' V07 §3.17's row 'a raised way over the palisade' adds '; a carried-down crossing station on the palisade kept with its raised gate or arch (V07 §3.5a (4))', and its test cell reads T-V7-48. T-V7-48's 'has 0 gates at supports' reads 'has 0 gates at supports but a carried-down crossing station's raised gate, kept with its tower carrying the deck', its CITY fixture's viaduct crossing the innermost ring at a raised gate. Model's END: §2.7's support step (6) (b) (iv) adds '— a crossing station carried down on the enceinte that becomes the palisade standing as (3) holds it (V07 §3.5a (4))'. Pipeline's END: §4.13's raised-way edge row `wall` takes the same clause.

claim: ONE FIX with VV78-r4-01 (T-V7-69 (e), V07 §4.5) and VV78-r4-02 (V07 §5.6 (3)'s text). This is the same R4-04 (b) class at the one V07 site neither names: T-V7-69 (c). The bar reads 'a disaster ruins whole units of `villageDisasterUnits` … every building of a returned unit drawing the ruined look and none outside', with no hand-over. Its fixtures include, from M-SF, a dossier fixture carrying each mapped condition: a disaster with its linked `reconstruction` condition (V08 §3.16 (7) (b)). §10.2 (f), §8.2, T-ER-27 and V07 §5.6 (3) itself hand each building over in the week a Works other than `decay` begins on it. A building under its rebuild is then drawn ruined by T-V7-69 (c) and rebuilt by every other unit. R4-04 graded that class MAJOR, and a correct build fails the bar.
required_change: T-V7-69 (c)'s 'every building of a returned unit drawing the ruined look and none outside' reads 'every building the look stands over (§10.2 (f): a building of a returned unit until V06 §3.22 (3)'s `crisisLookYields` turns true on it, a preview never handing over) drawing the ruined look, a building of a returned unit whose rebuild Works begin in the condition's weeks drawing its Works from that week, and none outside'; its dossier fixture adds a disaster whose rebuild Works begin on some of an end's buildings.

claim: R4-04 (b) makes every reader of a disaster look's damage, tone, lines and rows read one predicate: the look stands over a building of its units until V06 §3.22 (3)'s `crisisLookYields` turns true on it (base §10.2 (f)). §8.2 keeps a unit's `ruinTone` only 'while the look stands over any of its buildings', and V09's why card on a building shows `info.crisis.ruinedFor` only where `LooksAnswer.crises[].over` is true (§11.2). V07 §4.5's crisis line, rewritten this round, gives that row 'for a `VillageEnd` a disaster look ruins … while a crisis look stands at the viewer's key', read from `opts.view`'s `crises`, `week` and `looks`: that is the look's weeks, with no hand-over. V07 §5.6 (4) has the ruined look yield building by building to its rebuild's Works. So an end whose every building has begun its rebuild inside the condition's weeks draws no ruined tone and no building row, yet its own why card says 'For now: Ruined quarters, the mill-end fire, weeks 30–34'. This is two outcomes for one case, R4-04's class, which it graded major. R4-04's sweep did not list V07 §4.5, §5.6 (6) or T-V7-69 (e), and bar (e) passes the stale row.
required_change: V07 §4.5's crisis line: 'the answer for a `VillageEnd` a disaster look ruins and for a `VillageField` a famine look leaves bare carries' → 'the answer for a `VillageEnd` of a disaster look's units (§10.2 (d)) while the look stands over a building on its plots (`villageUnitPlots`; §10.2 (f): V06 §3.22 (3)'s `crisisLookYields` not yet true on it at `opts.view`'s week, a preview never handing over — as the end's `ruinTone` stands, §8.2) and for a `VillageField` a famine look leaves bare carries'. W74's input cell adds 'V06 §3.22 (3)'s `crisisLookYields` on the end's buildings (`villageUnitPlots`) for the crisis line'. V07 §5.6 (6): 'carries the crisis line on a ruined end and a bare field' → 'carries the crisis line on an end the disaster look stands over (§10.2 (f)) and on a bare field'. T-V7-69 (e): 'on an end a disaster look ruins' → 'on an end of a disaster look's units', and after 'and none otherwise' add ', an end every building of which has begun its rebuild's Works (the look standing over none of them, its `ruinTone` gone) among the none'.

claim: R4-04's two phrases are missing at three other V07 sites. Each is a restatement narrower in form; V07 §5.6 (3) defines the units and V06 §3.22 (3) and §8.2 are cited, so nothing built changes. (1) §5.6 (3)'s **The look** says 'a building whose rebuild Works has begun draws its Works instead (V06 §3.22 (3)'s `crisisLookYields`)'. That names only a rebuild and omits the predicate's 'other than a `decay` Works', 'unless finished before the overlay's `sinceWeek`' and 'a preview never hands over'. It also gives the units' tone without 'while the look stands over any of its buildings'. (2) §5.6 (5) says 'the ruined ends' tone'. (3) §3.17's row 'a crisis look over a hand-off epoch' says 'the village's ends after a hand-off down'. Both use 'ends' alone at the village rungs, where an end-less thorp's units are its toft groups (R4-04 (a)).
required_change: V07 §5.6 (3) **The look**: 'Every building on a returned unit's plots draws item 123's damage at `lookLevel` by severity, or at its own decay level where that is higher (V02's exterior, V03's plan; nothing stored), and the unit's plots' faces take §8.2's ruined tone at the city band; a building whose rebuild Works has begun draws its Works instead (V06 §3.22 (3)'s `crisisLookYields`).' → 'Every building on a returned unit's plots draws item 123's damage at `lookLevel` by severity, or at its own decay level where that is higher (V02's exterior, V03's plan; nothing stored), while the look stands over it (§10.2 (f): until V06 §3.22 (3)'s `crisisLookYields` turns true on it, then its Works; a preview never handing over), and the unit's plots' faces take §8.2's ruined tone at the city band while the look stands over any of its buildings.' §5.6 (5): 'the ruined ends' tone' → 'the ruined units' tone ((3))'. §3.17's row 'a crisis look over a hand-off epoch': 'the village's ends after a hand-off down' → 'V07 §5.6 (3)'s units (its ends, or an end-less thorp's toft groups) after a hand-off down'.
